gen_risks.description: Interoperability challenges between the Unique Social Registry (RSU) and other government databases may delay integrated targeting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a dedicated technical integration team, adopt open‑data standards, pilot test interfaces, and engage ANSSI and CIL for security and privacy compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will support the development of interoperable framework/platform where different databases and individual systems communicate...

gen_risks.description: Cybersecurity and data‑protection breaches could compromise beneficiary information in the RSU.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a Security Risk Assessment, implement a Security Management Plan, use encryption, regular security audits, and follow ANSSI guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: Will follow the security procedures elaborated by the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) and apply national data protection measures.

gen_risks.description: Administrative routines may cause procurement delays, slowing component rollout.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare a detailed procurement section in the Project Implementation Manual, set maximum timelines for each stage, and train staff on STEP procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Administrative routines may result in procurement delays, potentially affecting project implementation.

gen_risks.description: Procurement in fragile areas with few bidders could limit competition and raise prices or enable collusion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank flexibilities for fragile contexts, pre‑qualify local suppliers, bundle purchases across regions, and monitor price benchmarks.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement in fragile areas with few bidders can restrict competition and possibly increase prices and collusion risks.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient procurement capacity may lead to poor contract management and administration of large contracts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a full‑time procurement specialist, deliver intensive World Bank procurement training, and establish an accountability framework with regular reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Insufficient capacity can lead to poor contract management and administration of large contracts.

gen_risks.description: Weak financial‑management capacity in the PIU could cause fiduciary weaknesses.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified FM staff, adopt a FM manual, install accounting software, appoint an external auditor, and conduct semi‑annual audit reports.
gen_risks.evidence: The assessment found that the MFS currently does not have a PIU with FM arrangements... To mitigate these gaps, the project will recruit qualified FM staff.

gen_risks.description: Disbursement may be blocked if the Productive Grants Manual and required grant agreements are not adopted on time.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare the Productive Grants Manual and template agreements before effectiveness, train MFS staff on compliance, and monitor readiness quarterly.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawal shall be made... unless the Recipient has adopted the Productive Grants Manual and entered into two Productive Grant Agreements.

gen_risks.description: Delays in establishing the PIU and recruiting key staff may breach covenant deadlines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set internal recruitment milestones, allocate budget for staffing, use interim contracts if needed, and report progress to the steering committee monthly.
gen_risks.evidence: The Recipient shall, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, establish... a committee... The PIU shall include key staff... no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Escalating security threats could force suspension or adaptation of field activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop security SOPs, maintain a contingency plan with remote delivery options, partner with NGOs able to operate in high‑risk zones, and regularly reassess risk levels.
gen_risks.evidence: Security risks are significant and could escalate... Adaptations include decreasing sessions, remote tools, or suspending activity.

gen_risks.description: SEA/SH incidents (sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment) could cause reputational damage and harm beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an SEA/SH Action Plan, conduct mandatory training, enforce a code of conduct, and integrate SEA/SH reporting into the grievance mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: SEA/SH risk is Substantial... To mitigate this risk, the project will prepare an SEA/SH Action Plan and Grievance Mechanism.

gen_risks.description: Grievance redress mechanism may fail to resolve complaints within stipulated timeframes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign a dedicated GRM officer, set clear SLA targets, track all cases in the MIS, and publish quarterly performance reports.
gen_risks.evidence: Grievance addressed within the stipulated timeframe (Percentage) is an indicator.

gen_risks.description: Ongoing conflict and fragility could disrupt implementation and increase costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Leverage the Contingent Emergency Response Component, maintain a security specialist in the PIU, and coordinate closely with CONASUR and security forces.
gen_risks.evidence: The project is flagged as Fragile State(s) and Conflict... includes Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC).

gen_risks.description: Construction of warehouses may cause water and soil pollution from waste.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct an ESIA, enforce a waste‑management plan, use best‑practice construction methods, and monitor runoff regularly.
gen_risks.evidence: Key E&S risks include water and soil pollution from solid and liquid waste at construction and rehabilitation sites.

gen_risks.description: Occupational health and safety hazards could affect workers at construction and field sites.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop an OHS plan, provide PPE and safety training, conduct regular site inspections, and report incidents promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: Key E&S risks include occupational health and safety of workers.

gen_risks.description: High turnover or insufficient capacity of PIU staff may impair project coordination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer competitive salaries, career‑development pathways, and performance‑based incentives; conduct periodic capacity assessments.
gen_risks.evidence: The PIU will be established prior to the project’s effective date and will recruit key staff.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related shocks could reduce beneficiary income and undermine project outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilient livelihood options, strengthen early warning systems, and allow flexible re‑targeting of assistance.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change also severely undermines food security... shocks undermine food and income security, forcing households to adopt negative coping strategies.

gen_risks.description: Declining humanitarian funding may limit resources for IDP support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Increase national ownership, diversify funding sources, and leverage private‑sector partnerships to sustain IDP assistance.
gen_risks.evidence: Recent cuts in humanitarian funding have reduced support for IDPs... declining humanitarian financing.

gen_risks.description: Large and ongoing IDP flows could complicate registration and targeting in the RSU.
gen_risks.mitigation: Scale up mobile registration teams, strengthen coordination with CONASUR, and prioritize data‑validation mechanisms for displaced populations.
gen_risks.evidence: The deteriorating security situation has led to internal displacement, about 2 million IDPs... RSU aims to register IDPs.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is assessed to be Substantial. The uncertain political and governance context provides a challenge to long-term development policy. Adaptive social protection systems are still nascent and will require continued political commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The team, guided by the management, will continue its high-level policy dialogue at central and decentralized levels and ensure continuous advocacy and communication.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed to be Substantial. Fiscal space remains constrained by elevated security spending and tighter financing conditions, which increase the risk of reduced budget allocations and delayed counterpart funding for new priorities and reforms, including social protection and the PAMPV. Macroeconomic risks also arise from exogenous factors, including current conflict in the Middle East which can result in a surge in oil prices and put inflationary pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: Other programs such as the International Monetary Fund program and the World Bank's technical assistance on tax expenditure under the Sustainable Development Finance Policy can help expand fiscal space, partially mitigating these risks.

gt_risks.description: Sector strategy and policies risks are considered to be Substantial. Sectoral strategies and policies remain nascent, and the Government's budget allocation to operationalize the PAMPV remains unclear. Also, sectoral decisions are at times taken abruptly and can heavily affect implementation (for example, the suspension of cash transfers in 2023 led to an increased focus on economic inclusion, and the newly emerged priority of the CONASUR/IDPs led to the revision of the fiche de projet of this project).
gt_risks.mitigation: In parallel with high-level policy dialogue, the project supports strategic communications, adopts an agile approach, and provides technical assistance to promote evidence-based decision-making (with support from SASPP, the Social Protection Response MDTF, and the State and Peacebuilding Fund).

gt_risks.description: Overall fiduciary risks are considered as Substantial, as described in section IV.B and annex 2, based on financial assessment and procurement assessment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project preparation fund (Grant Facility for Project Preparation) has been used not only to prepare mitigation measures to address these risks but will also elevate the project readiness (for example, effectiveness-linked actions including FM and procurement staffing and initiating the procurement packages for the first 18-months' implementation priorities) to improve the project performance.

gt_risks.description: Other risks related to insecurity are rated as High. The deteriorating and volatile security situation—particularly in regions with high poverty, displacement, and food insecurity that are project intervention areas—will likely be an important risk. The project will also address other risks related to protection of personal data: for Component 2 on social registry and interoperability, activities will be guided by the Information System Security Policy (ISSP) document developed by the ANSSI, to ensure confidentiality of households registered in the RSU.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project activities will be adjusted based on the security situation (see annex 3), and the PIU will be also staffed with a security specialist and a security management plan will be developed. To remain engaged, the project will also rely on remote delivery/monitoring, partnering with local representation (NGOs, UN agencies). The ST-RSU will conduct capacity-building activities, including training sessions and awareness campaigns, to strengthen users' ability to manage and protect households' personal data.
